- Model tends to overestimate prices in early forecast periods, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 1–3%.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots the true value in the following days; apply a downward correction of 2–5% for the next 3–5 days.
- Model underestimates prices during prolonged downward trends; increase forecast by 1–2% during such periods.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias — forecasts too quickly revert to historical averages; delay mean reversion by 2–4 days unless strong macro signals exist.
- Model consistently underestimates true values in the final 5–7 days of the forecast horizon; add a 1–3% upward bias to the last 5–7 days.
- Model overreacts to short-term volatility; smooth out forecast volatility by reducing standard deviation by 20–30% unless confirmed by macro indicators.
- When true values show a clear downward trend after a peak, model often fails to recognize the trend’s persistence; adjust forecast to reflect a 1–2% slower decline than model suggests.
